title: Async Streams and Channels
summary: Data that arrives over time - IAsyncEnumerable with yield return and await foreach, cancellation with [EnumeratorCancellation], System.Threading.Channels for producers and consumers, bounded channels and back-pressure, and pipelines of async stages.

cards.q: When is an `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` better than a `Task<List<T>>`?
cards.a:
When results arrive over time and can be handled one by one

With `await foreach`, the consumer can start on the first item as soon as it arrives. A `Task<List<T>>` makes the caller wait until every item is ready.

cards.q: What does a bounded channel do when it is full and its mode is `Wait`?
cards.a:
The writer's `WriteAsync` waits until a reader makes room

Waiting is back-pressure: a fast writer is slowed to the reader's pace. Dropping items is what the `DropNewest`, `DropOldest` and `DropWrite` modes do.

cards.q: How does a consumer's await foreach over channel.Reader.ReadAllAsync() know to stop?
cards.a:
When the writer calls Complete() and the channel is empty

`Complete()` marks the end of the data; `ReadAllAsync` finishes once the remaining items are read.
